summary: Each method call must return one number, and the accepted closures perform only one fixed-size state update, leaving no genuine slower principal class for scaling.

optimality.argument: Every operation must produce one numeric result and therefore requires Omega(1) work. Each accepted method reads and updates at most one captured number using a fixed number of operations, giving O(1) time per call.

replacement_checks.evidence: Returning the required numeric result imposes a constant lower bound on every method invocation.
Increment and decrement perform one arithmetic update, while reset performs one assignment to the captured initialization value.
Cases cover zero calls, every operation, repeated resets, alternating updates, crossing zero, and both initialization bounds.
